title: Watchers
description: Is the watching machinery itself still running? Every other board asks whether the WATCHED thing is healthy; this one asks whether the watchers are alive. Built on node_systemd_timer_last_trigger_seconds plus the textfile run-timestamp family. NOT an alert console: the stack is collection-only (no vmalert, no alertmanager), so nothing here records that an alert FIRED — only that the machinery that would have fired it is still turning.

panels.title: Watchers overdue
panels.description: Curated watcher timers whose overdue factor (time since last trigger ÷ the tier's expected cadence) has reached 3×. Healthy watchers sit at or below 1×, so any count here means a watcher has stopped firing. Green at 0; amber at the first, red at the second. Read together with “Watchers not writing”: overdue here means the timer itself stopped.

targets.expr:
count(
  (label_set(label_replace((time() - (node_systemd_timer_last_trigger_seconds{name=~"monitoring-unit-state-check[.]timer|monitoring-git-annex-alert-check[.]timer"} > 0)) / 60, "host", "$1", "instance", "([^.:]+).*"), "cadence", "60s")
  or label_set(label_replace((time() - (node_systemd_timer_last_trigger_seconds{name=~"book-filer[.]timer|deadman-heartbeat[.]timer|git-annex-metrics-.*[.]timer|backup-restic-status[.]timer|beets-import[.]timer"} > 0)) / 300, "host", "$1", "instance", "([^.:]+).*"), "cadence", "5m")
  or label_set(label_replace((time() - (node_systemd_timer_last_trigger_seconds{name=~"music-sync[.]timer|blocky-service-hosts[.]timer"} > 0)) / 1800, "host", "$1", "instance", "([^.:]+).*"), "cadence", "30m")
  or label_set(label_replace((time() - (node_systemd_timer_last_trigger_seconds{name=~"monitoring-dmarc-alert-check[.]timer|monitoring-tlsrpt-alert-check[.]timer|monitoring-tlsrpt-poll[.]timer"} > 0)) / 3600, "host", "$1", "instance", "([^.:]+).*"), "cadence", "1h")
  or label_set(label_replace((time() - (node_systemd_timer_last_trigger_seconds{name=~"monitoring-secret-expiry-check[.]timer|nixos-metrics[.]timer"} > 0)) / 86400, "host", "$1", "instance", "([^.:]+).*"), "cadence", "1d"))
  >= 3
) or vector(0)

panels.title: Watchers not writing
panels.description: Of the three watchers that publish their own run timestamp (git-annex-metrics, backup-restic-status, book-filer), how many last wrote more than 15 minutes ago — 3× their 5-minute cadence. A count here with “Watchers overdue” at 0 is the diagnostic case: the timer is firing but the job is failing before it writes. The other 18 of the 27 tracked timer series have no such cross-check.

targets.expr:
count(
  (label_set(label_replace(time() - git_annex_check_timestamp_seconds{user="git-annex"}, "host", "$1", "instance", "([^.:]+).*"), "watcher", "git-annex-metrics")
  or label_set(label_replace(time() - backup_restic_check_timestamp_seconds, "host", "$1", "instance", "([^.:]+).*"), "watcher", "backup-restic-status")
  or label_set(label_replace(time() - books_inbox_last_run_timestamp_seconds, "host", "$1", "instance", "([^.:]+).*"), "watcher", "book-filer"))
  >= 900
) or vector(0)

panels.title: Books stuck in inbox
panels.description: Files the #144 book filer could not file, summed across all four reasons (bad-path, collision, no-metadata, unsupported-format). Each one sits in the inbox until a human intervenes — the filer keeps running, so no other panel goes red. Amber at the first, red at five. Breakdown in the Book filer row below.

panels.title: Watchers reporting
panels.description: How many curated watcher timers are currently reporting at all. Deliberately unthresholded — the expected count is not a constant: it moves when a host is added, when an on-demand host is asleep, or when a profile is enabled. Today it is 27. A sustained DROP is the signal (a watcher that vanished rather than went stale); watch it against the tier trend below.

panels.title: Watcher freshness — overdue factor
panels.description: Every curated watcher timer on the fleet, ranked by how far past its expected cadence it is. Overdue factor = time since last trigger ÷ the cadence constant for its tier, so a 60-second watcher and a daily one are directly comparable and the worst offender always sorts to the top. Bands: green below 3×, amber at 3×, red at 6×. Healthy watchers read at or below 1×. The cadence shown is the SLOWEST declared interval in the tier, so the factor is conservative and never over-flags. GOTCHA: only SYSTEM timers appear here — sawtoothShark runs git-annex-metrics as a home-manager USER timer, which node-exporter's systemd collector cannot see, so it is absent by design rather than dead. A host missing a row for a watcher it never ran (porcupineFish and rk1a run no monitoring-* alerters) is likewise normal.

panels.title: Overdue factor by tier
panels.description: The worst overdue factor in each cadence tier over time — the trend view behind the table above. Cardinality is deliberately reduced from 27 watchers to five tiers so every series can hold a pinned house colour (the style forbids a 9th hue). A tier riding at or just above 1× is healthy; a line that ramps and never comes back down is a watcher that has stopped. GOTCHA: at raw resolution this panel is an unreadable picket fence — the factor resets to 0 on every trigger, so a 60-second watcher draws ~1400 teeth across a 24-hour window (the same trap #160 hit with the Pi's bang-bang fans). Taking max_over_time over a 10-minute window keeps the peak, which is the whole signal, and drops the teeth. The dashed line marks the 3× amber cutoff; the axis is soft-capped there so a healthy board is not drawn on a degenerate scale.

targets.expr:
max by (cadence) (
  max_over_time(
    (
label_set(label_replace((time() - (node_systemd_timer_last_trigger_seconds{name=~"monitoring-unit-state-check[.]timer|monitoring-git-annex-alert-check[.]timer"} > 0)) / 60, "host", "$1", "instance", "([^.:]+).*"), "cadence", "60s")
  or label_set(label_replace((time() - (node_systemd_timer_last_trigger_seconds{name=~"book-filer[.]timer|deadman-heartbeat[.]timer|git-annex-metrics-.*[.]timer|backup-restic-status[.]timer|beets-import[.]timer"} > 0)) / 300, "host", "$1", "instance", "([^.:]+).*"), "cadence", "5m")
  or label_set(label_replace((time() - (node_systemd_timer_last_trigger_seconds{name=~"music-sync[.]timer|blocky-service-hosts[.]timer"} > 0)) / 1800, "host", "$1", "instance", "([^.:]+).*"), "cadence", "30m")
  or label_set(label_replace((time() - (node_systemd_timer_last_trigger_seconds{name=~"monitoring-dmarc-alert-check[.]timer|monitoring-tlsrpt-alert-check[.]timer|monitoring-tlsrpt-poll[.]timer"} > 0)) / 3600, "host", "$1", "instance", "([^.:]+).*"), "cadence", "1h")
  or label_set(label_replace((time() - (node_systemd_timer_last_trigger_seconds{name=~"monitoring-secret-expiry-check[.]timer|nixos-metrics[.]timer"} > 0)) / 86400, "host", "$1", "instance", "([^.:]+).*"), "cadence", "1d")
    )[10m]
  )
)

panels.title: Watchers that publish their own run time
panels.description: The three watchers that write a run timestamp of their own, so their WORK can be checked independently of their TIMER: git-annex-metrics, backup-restic-status and book-filer. All three run on a 5-minute cadence, so one absolute band serves them all — green below 15 minutes, amber at 15 (3×), red at 30 (6×). The diagnostic read is the cross-check against the table above: a watcher that is FRESH there but stale here is firing on schedule and failing before it writes — a failure no other board can see. Only 9 of the 27 tracked timer series can be checked this way; the other 18 publish no run timestamp of their own. GOTCHA: filtered to user="git-annex", so sawtoothShark's home-manager pictures repo is excluded here for the same reason it is absent above.

targets.expr:
label_set(label_replace(time() - git_annex_check_timestamp_seconds{user="git-annex"}, "host", "$1", "instance", "([^.:]+).*"), "watcher", "git-annex-metrics")
  or label_set(label_replace(time() - backup_restic_check_timestamp_seconds, "host", "$1", "instance", "([^.:]+).*"), "watcher", "backup-restic-status")
  or label_set(label_replace(time() - books_inbox_last_run_timestamp_seconds, "host", "$1", "instance", "([^.:]+).*"), "watcher", "book-filer")

panels.title: Stuck files by reason
panels.description: Why the #144 book filer could not file a dropped book, one tile per reason. bad-path = the file landed somewhere the filer will not touch; collision = a book of that name already exists; no-metadata = no usable EPUB metadata to file by; unsupported-format = Stump cannot index it (MOBI is the known case — PDF is fine). Green at 0, amber at the first, red at five. Empty is healthy, and all four read 0 today.

panels.title: Stuck files over time
panels.description: Stuck-file count per reason as a trend, so a slow accumulation is visible rather than only the instantaneous total in the glance. A flat zero is the healthy shape — the axis is soft-capped at 5 so a healthy board does not render on a degenerate scale. A step that never comes back down means nobody has cleared the inbox.
